comments.body: I would also be interested if someone knows the reason! I've noticed the same phenomenon, and it would be great to be able to make minor changes to a configuration without rebuilding the entire thing from scratch!
This is an unfortunate limitation of how verilator works. When you change the verilog in any way, verilator will create an entirely new set of C++ files, so they will all get rebuilt.

comments.body:
I have the same problem.
It seems the requirement failed in pwm.scala:

``` scala
trait PWMTLModule extends Module with HasRegMap {
  val io: PWMTLBundle
  implicit val p: Parameters
  def params: PWMParams

  val w = params.beatBytes * 8
  require(w <= 32)  //FAILED HERE
  ...
}
```

I am new to Scala/Chisel and I can't figure out how does this code work.
It seem that `PWMTLModule` defines an abstract function `params` but not implement it?
And if I assign `w` a fixed number, say, 4, it will compile.
Can anyone give some advices about this problem? 
Thanks a lot!

Sounds like it might be a mismatch between beatBytes coming from rocket-chip and what the PWM module wants.

Are you just using master of this repo?
Yeap, I just using the master branch and its submodules.

I think the problem is that, when XLen is configured as 64-bit, beatBytes equals to 8.
But here w is expected to be smaller than 32, so the requirement failed.
If I modify the code as follows, it will work: 

``` scala
trait PWMTLModule extends HasRegMap {
  val io: PWMTLBundle
  implicit val p: Parameters
  def params: PWMParams

  val w = params.beatBytes * 8
  require(w <= 64)

  // ...
  
  //modify register map to avoid address overlap
  regmap(
    0x00 -> Seq(
      RegField(w, period)),
    0x08 -> Seq(
      RegField(w, duty)),
    0x016 -> Seq(
      RegField(1, enable)))
}
```

Using 64bit register for PWM is waste and totally unneccessary.
but looks like rocketchip have bug regarding using different periphery register width from xbar width.
Sorry I didn't address this issue until now. I'm just going to fix the width at 32 so that we don't have this issue of changing bus widths.

It looks like the recent update to Scala 2.13 (#1303) broke the Chisel Hierarchy API. It looks like we'll need an extra `scalac` option to fix the issue.

```scala
import chisel3.experimental.hierarchy.{Definition, Instance, instantiable, public}

@instantiable
class AddOne(width: Int) extends Module {
  @public val in  = IO(Input(UInt(width.W)))
  @public val out = IO(Output(UInt(width.W)))
  out := in + 1.U
}

class AddTwo(width: Int) extends Module {
  val in  = IO(Input(UInt(width.W)))
  val out = IO(Output(UInt(width.W)))
  val addOneDef = Definition(new AddOne(width))
  val i0 = Instance(addOneDef)
  val i1 = Instance(addOneDef)
  i0.in := in
  i1.in := i0.out
  out   := i1.out
}
```

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the above code to compile without error. In fact, if you add `"-Ymacro-annotations"` to `scalacOptions` in `build.sbt`, the build works. I'm not sure if there are other Scala compiler options that we're missing, but that one certainly seems necessary.

title: Update QEMU for binutils 2.36 (Ubuntu 21.04)
body:
<!-- choose one -->
**Impact**: software

**Description**
I recently hit the exact problem reported in this patch on the qemu-stable list, as I was compiling QEMU as part of Chipyard (at commit 5129bc7da5093f1d289c2fed27673cf51024eb0d) on Ubuntu 21.04:

https://lists.nongnu.org/archive/html/qemu-stable/2020-12/msg00015.html

> Recent binutils changes dropping unsupported options [1] caused a build
> issue in regard to the optionroms.
> 
>   ld -m elf_i386 -T /<<PKGBUILDDIR>>/pc-bios/optionrom//flat.lds -no-pie \
>     -s -o multiboot.img multiboot.o
>   ld.bfd: Error: unable to disambiguate: -no-pie (did you mean --no-pie ?)
> 
> This isn't really a regression in ld.bfd, filing the bug upstream
> revealed that this never worked as a ld flag [2] - in fact it seems we
> were by accident setting --nmagic).
> 
> Since it never had the wanted effect this usage of LDFLAGS_NOPIE, should be
> droppable without any effect. This also is the only use-case of
> LDFLAGS_NOPIE
> in .mak, therefore we can also remove it from being added there.
> 
> [1]: https://sourceware.org/git/?p=binutils-gdb.git;a=commit;h=983d925d
> [2]: https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=27050#c5

The patch was applied in this commit: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/commit/bbd2d5a8120771ec59b86a80a1f51884e0a26e53

And partially reverted in this commit: https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/commit/ffd205ef2901bd

Because Chipyard is pinning the `toolchains/qemu` git submodule at v5.0.0, it has neither of these fixes, but if Chipyard updates the git submodule to qemu v6.0.1, it will get both of these fixes.

To test the new version of QEMU, I updated the git submodule to v6.0.1 locally, and re-ran `scripts/build-toolchains.sh`. It gave me the following error and exited without building QEMU:

```
==>  PLEASE REMOVE qemu URL-REWRITING from scripts/build-toolchains.sh. It is no longer needed!
```

So, I removed the url rewriting (put in place to avoid git.qemu.org, which no longer exists) using the attached patch, and the toolchain build completes successfully.

[patch_drop_url_rewriting.txt](https://github.com/ucb-bar/chipyard/files/7564537/patch_drop_url_rewriting.txt)
:

**What is a motivating example for changing the behavior?**

QEMU v5.0.0 fails to compile Ubuntu 21.04 or any later version, because binutils 2.36 no longer accepts the invalid ld flag `-no-pie`.
